Compare MMM fits across different k

Source: R/mmm.R
compare_mmm.Rd

compare_mmm() fits a mixed Markov model with build_mmm() for each number of subgroups in k and returns one row per fit with its log-likelihood, information criteria (AIC, BIC, ICL), overall average posterior probability (AvePP), entropy and convergence. Every fit uses the same data and the same build_mmm() settings.

Lower AIC, BIC and ICL indicate more support relative to the other fits. ICL adds a penalty for uncertain classification to BIC, so it favours subgroups that separate cleanly (Biernacki, Celeux & Govaert, 2000); AvePP and entropy describe that separation within each fit. The criteria do not settle k on their own: check that every fit converged, that the subgroups' transition matrices of the chosen fit differ in interpretable ways (summary() of that fit prints them), and, when the criteria keep falling at the largest k, extend the range.

Usage

compare_mmm(
  data,
  k = 2:5,
  return_fits = FALSE,
  n_starts = 50L,
  max_iter = 200L,
  tol = 1e-06,
  smooth = 0.01,
  seed = NULL,
  covariates = NULL,
  covariate_effect = c("em", "posthoc"),
  estimator = c("auto", "firth", "multinom", "chisq")
)

# S3 method for class 'mmm_compare'
print(x, ...)

# S3 method for class 'mmm_compare'
summary(object, ...)

# S3 method for class 'mmm_compare'
plot(x, ...)

Arguments

data

The sequences, in any form build_mmm() accepts: a wide data frame, a netobject or cograph_network built from sequences, or a tna model.

k

The numbers of subgroups to fit, a non-empty vector of whole numbers of at least 2; one model is fitted per value. Default 2:5.

return_fits

Whether to keep the fitted models. With TRUE, the net_mmm fits are attached to the result as its "fits" attribute, a list named by k, so the chosen model needs no second run of the EM. Default FALSE, which returns only the comparison table.

n_starts

How many starting configurations to try, a positive whole number. More starts make it likelier that the best local maximum is found. Default 50.

max_iter

The most EM iterations a start may run, a positive whole number. Default 200.

tol

The convergence tolerance: EM stops when the log-likelihood changes by less than this between iterations (with covariate_effect = "em", also when its relative change does). A finite positive number; default 1e-6.

smooth

A pseudo-count added to every transition count before the matrices are estimated, so a transition unseen in a subgroup gets a small probability instead of zero. A finite non-negative number; default 0.01.

seed

A seed for reproducible starts, applied afresh to each fit (every k starts from the same random state). Default NULL.

covariates

Variables describing each sequence (such as a course or a grade), given as a column name, a character vector of names, a one-sided formula or a data frame, as in build_clusters(). For a netobject, names are looked up in its metadata first, so a typical call is build_mmm(net, k = 3, covariates = "session_label"). How they enter the model is set by covariate_effect. Default NULL.

covariate_effect

How covariates enter the model. "em" (default) makes the mixing proportions depend on them during EM, so they shape the subgroups found and add (k - 1) * p parameters for p covariate columns; rows with a missing covariate are dropped first, with a warning. "posthoc" fits a plain mixture on every sequence and relates the covariates to the subgroups only afterwards, with a multinomial logit, so neither their values nor their missingness change the subgroups. Ignored without covariates.

estimator

How the after-fit multinomial logit is estimated; it never affects the EM. "auto" (default) uses Firth's penalised likelihood (brglm2::brmultinom(), finite under separation) when a cell of the subgroup-by-covariate table has fewer than 5 sequences, and nnet::multinom() otherwise. "firth" and "multinom" force one of them ("multinom" warns about separation risk), and "chisq" runs descriptive tests instead of a logit. build_clusters() has the details. Ignored without covariates.

x

For the print() and plot() methods: an mmm_compare table.

...

For the print(), summary() and plot() methods: not used; any extra argument raises an error.

object

For the summary() method: an mmm_compare table.

Value

An mmm_compare object, a data frame with one row per value of k. print() shows the table with a best column marking the lowest BIC ("<-- BIC") and, when it falls on a different row, the lowest ICL ("<-- ICL"), and returns that marked table invisibly. summary() returns the same table as a plain data frame with a best column holding "BIC", "ICL" or ""; when one row has both minima it is marked "BIC" only. plot() draws BIC, AIC and ICL against k, and returns the ggplot invisibly after printing it. The table's columns are k, log_likelihood, AIC, BIC, ICL, AvePP, Entropy and converged; return_fits = TRUE adds the "fits" attribute.

References

Biernacki, C., Celeux, G., & Govaert, G. (2000). Assessing a mixture model for clustering with the integrated completed likelihood. IEEE Transactions on Pattern Analysis and Machine Intelligence, 22(7), 719–725. doi:10.1109/34.865189

See also

build_mmm(), cluster_mmm()

Examples

seqs <- data.frame(V1 = sample(c("A","B","C"), 30, TRUE),
                   V2 = sample(c("A","B","C"), 30, TRUE))
comp <- compare_mmm(seqs, k = 2:3, n_starts = 1, max_iter = 10, seed = 1)
comp
#> MMM Model Comparison
#> 
#>  k log_likelihood AIC      BIC      ICL      AvePP     Entropy   converged
#>  2 -62.32972      158.6594 182.4798 184.6518 0.9647836 0.2121121  TRUE    
#>  3 -62.32987      176.6597 213.0909 217.2174 0.9343265 0.2487206 FALSE    
#>  best   
#>  <-- BIC
#>         
# \donttest{
seqs <- data.frame(
  V1 = sample(LETTERS[1:3], 30, TRUE), V2 = sample(LETTERS[1:3], 30, TRUE),
  V3 = sample(LETTERS[1:3], 30, TRUE), V4 = sample(LETTERS[1:3], 30, TRUE)
)
comp <- compare_mmm(seqs, k = 2:3, seed = 42)
print(comp)
#> MMM Model Comparison
#> 
#>  k log_likelihood AIC      BIC      ICL      AvePP     Entropy    converged
#>  2 -120.8229      275.6458 299.4661 299.9897 0.9920817 0.03537724 TRUE     
#>  3 -115.1023      282.2045 318.6357 319.2157 0.9908021 0.03304310 TRUE     
#>  best   
#>  <-- BIC
#>         

# Retain the fits so the chosen model needs no re-run; summary() marks
# the minimum-BIC and minimum-ICL rows in its `best` column.
comp_with_fits <- compare_mmm(seqs, k = 2:3, seed = 42, return_fits = TRUE)
summary(comp_with_fits)
#>   k log_likelihood      AIC      BIC      ICL     AvePP    Entropy converged
#> 1 2      -120.8229 275.6458 299.4661 299.9897 0.9920817 0.03537724      TRUE
#> 2 3      -115.1023 282.2045 318.6357 319.2157 0.9908021 0.03304310      TRUE
#>   best
#> 1  BIC
#> 2     
# }
